examples: 이번이 좋은 기회라고 생각해요.
I think this is a good opportunity.
이라고 생각하다 means think that
저는 외국에서 일할 기회를 잡고 싶어요.
I want to seize a chance to work abroad.
기회를 잡다 collocation
좋은 기회를 놓쳐서 너무 아쉬워요.
I missed a good chance, so I really regret it.
놓치다 with 를
nuance: 기회 means an opportunity or chance to do something, often one that may not come again. The natural verbs are 기회를 잡다 to seize it and 기회를 놓치다 to miss it, rather than 기회를 하다. 기회가 되면 is a common phrase meaning if I get the chance.
mistakes: Saying 기회를 하다 instead of 기회를 잡다 or 기회가 있다
Marking it 기회를 있다 instead of 기회가 있다

examples: 그분은 일에 대한 태도가 정말 진지해요.
That person's attitude toward work is really serious.
에 대한 means toward
면접에서는 태도가 무엇보다 중요해요.
In an interview, attitude matters more than anything.
무엇보다 means above all
실수한 뒤에 태도를 바꿔서 다행이에요.
I'm relieved he changed his attitude after the mistake.
태도를 바꾸다 collocation
nuance: 태도 means the attitude or stance someone shows through behavior, especially toward work, people, or a situation. It is often paired with 에 대한 to mean attitude toward something. Unlike 자세, which can be a physical posture, 태도 is mostly about one's mental and behavioral disposition.
mistakes: Confusing 태도 with 자세 when 자세 means physical posture
Saying 태도를 좋다 instead of 태도가 좋다

examples: 이 책은 내용이 조금 어려워요.
This book's content is a little difficult.
내용이 with 이
회의 내용을 간단히 정리해서 보냈어요.
I summarized the meeting content briefly and sent it.
내용을 정리하다 collocation
문자 내용을 다시 한번 확인해 주세요.
Please check the content of the message once more.
내용을 with 을
nuance: 내용 means the content or substance of something like a book, message, lecture, or conversation, as opposed to its outer form. It often pairs with 정리하다 to summarize and 이해하다 to understand. Use 내용 for what is inside, not the physical container, which would be 상자 or 봉투.
mistakes: Saying 내용을 어렵다 instead of 내용이 어렵다
Using 내용 for a physical container instead of the substance inside

examples: 이 가게는 빵 종류가 정말 많아요.
This shop has a really wide variety of bread.
종류가 많다 collocation
어떤 종류의 음악을 좋아하세요?
What kind of music do you like?
종류의 modifies 음악
같은 종류의 제품인데 가격이 달라요.
They're the same kind of product but the prices differ.
같은 종류의 means same type of
nuance: 종류 means a kind, type, or category of something, and 종류가 많다 means there are many varieties. To say what kind of X, Koreans use 어떤 종류의 X. It is more about classification than 가지, which is used when counting items, as in 두 가지.
mistakes: Saying 종류를 많다 instead of 종류가 많다
Forgetting 의 in 어떤 종류의 음악

examples: 이 학원은 수업 수준이 꽤 높아요.
This academy's class level is quite high.
수준이 높다 collocation
제 한국어 수준은 아직 중급이에요.
My Korean level is still intermediate.
중급 means intermediate
꾸준히 연습해서 실력 수준을 높이고 싶어요.
I want to raise my skill level by practicing steadily.
수준을 높이다 collocation
nuance: 수준 means the level or standard of something such as ability, quality, or living conditions. 수준이 높다 and 수준이 낮다 describe how high or low that level is. It often follows another noun, as in 생활 수준 or 한국어 수준, to specify what is being measured.
mistakes: Saying 수준을 높다 instead of 수준이 높다
Confusing 수준 with 단계, which means a step or stage in a sequence

examples: 중고차라서 상태를 꼼꼼히 확인했어요.
Since it's a used car, I checked its condition carefully.
상태를 확인하다 collocation
요즘 잠을 못 자서 건강 상태가 안 좋아요.
I haven't slept well lately, so my health is poor.
건강 상태 collocation
냉장고 안 음식 상태를 한번 봐 주세요.
Please take a look at the state of the food in the fridge.
음식 상태 means food condition
nuance: 상태 means the current state or condition of a person, object, or situation at a given moment. It frequently follows another noun, as in 건강 상태 or 상태가 좋다, to describe how something is doing. Unlike 상황, which refers to a broader circumstance or situation, 상태 focuses on the condition of one specific thing.
mistakes: Saying 상태를 좋다 instead of 상태가 좋다
Confusing 상태 with 상황, which means a broader situation

examples: 오랜만에 친구의 밝은 모습을 봐서 기뻤어요.
I was glad to see my friend looking cheerful after so long.
모습을 보다 collocation
이 동네는 십 년 전과 모습이 많이 달라졌어요.
This neighborhood's appearance has changed a lot from ten years ago.
모습이 달라지다 collocation
열심히 일하는 부모님의 모습이 떠올랐어요.
The image of my hardworking parents came to mind.
모습이 떠오르다 collocation
nuance: 모습 means the visible appearance, figure, or image of a person or scene, including how someone looks or behaves at a moment. It often appears with a modifying clause, as in 일하는 모습 meaning the sight of someone working. It is broader and more visual than 얼굴, covering one's whole look and manner rather than just the face.
mistakes: Saying 모습을 보이다 when you mean 모습이 보이다 for something being visible
Using 모습 only for the face instead of the whole appearance

examples: 이 카페는 분위기가 정말 편안해요.
This cafe has a really relaxing atmosphere.
분위기가 좋다 collocation
회식 분위기를 띄우려고 농담을 했어요.
I made a joke to liven up the company dinner.
분위기를 띄우다 collocation
갑자기 분위기가 어색해져서 조용히 있었어요.
The mood suddenly turned awkward, so I stayed quiet.
분위기가 어색해지다 collocation
nuance: 분위기 means the atmosphere or mood of a place, gathering, or situation. 분위기가 좋다 describes a pleasant vibe, and 분위기를 띄우다 means to liven things up. It refers to the collective feeling in the air, which is different from 기분, the personal feeling of one individual.
mistakes: Confusing 분위기 with 기분, which is one person's mood
Saying 분위기를 좋다 instead of 분위기가 좋다

examples: 이번 시험 범위가 생각보다 넓어요.
This exam's scope is wider than I thought.
시험 범위 collocation
예산 범위 안에서 가구를 골랐어요.
I chose furniture within the budget range.
범위 안에서 means within the range
발표 주제의 범위를 조금 줄이는 게 좋겠어요.
It would be better to narrow the scope of the presentation topic a bit.
범위를 줄이다 means narrow the scope
nuance: 범위 means the range or scope that something covers, such as an exam syllabus, a budget, or a topic. 범위가 넓다 means broad and 범위가 좁다 means narrow, while 범위 안에서 means within a certain range. It is a fairly formal, written-leaning noun common in study and work contexts.
mistakes: Saying 범위를 넓다 instead of 범위가 넓다
Confusing 범위 with 사이, which means the space or relationship between two points

examples: 혼자서 할 수 있는 일에는 한계가 있어요.
There's a limit to what I can do alone.
한계가 있다 collocation
야근이 계속돼서 체력의 한계를 느꼈어요.
With the overtime continuing, I felt the limit of my stamina.
한계를 느끼다 collocation
꾸준히 노력하면 한계를 넘을 수 있어요.
If you keep trying steadily, you can go beyond your limits.
한계를 넘다 collocation
nuance: 한계 means a limit or boundary beyond which something cannot go, often used for ability, stamina, or patience. 한계를 느끼다 means to feel that you have reached your limit, and 한계를 넘다 means to push past it. It is more abstract than 끝, which simply means the end point of something.
mistakes: Saying 한계를 있다 instead of 한계가 있다
Confusing 한계 with 끝, which just means the end
